I suggest a short circle in the car park afterwards, then off to one of Duffield's excellent pubs (there is a choice of two, with a car park between them, free on Sundays). If coming by bus, get off at the Baptist Church and walk down the lane.

Trail part of the Matlock Big Weekend -see Events link. Normal QH3 Sunday trail open to all. Matlock is served by bus and train services. The pub has no car park so if coming by car plan your car parking carefully. Allow for at least 3 hours parking and make sure you get there in plenty of time for a 11 a.m. start. Artist Corner and the Railway Station car parks are likely the best option long stay car parks. Runner and walker trails.

A friendly pub with adjoining microbrewery. Formerly the Blue Bell. You are promised a lovely scenic trail (5.75 miles with a walkers option) with lots of historical insterest. Buses from East Midlands Airport stop right outside, though unfortunately for the reverse direction the stop is in the town centre 400 metres away.
The pub have asked for us to park on the roads near the pub as Sunday is their busiest time

It will be a perfect hash of 5 miles and a shorter route for the walkers, some virgin trail has been found and less mud than the last hash. Come and join the hares Ballcrusher and B*gger next Sunday for a cracking hash in the Derbyshire

Come and join your hares B*gger and Goblin for this year's Jingle Balls run around Kegworth, with a perfect 5 mile trail for the quicker ones and a perfect 3-miler for walkers. Please come properly attired - Christmas hat is mandatory plus anything red and/or jingly. The Nottingham sklylink bus goes to the East Midland Gateway hub just over the motorway from Kegworth. The Derby to Leicester Sklylink goes through the village. If travelling by car on M1 come off at 24 and Please park at the bottom of the car park

hares: Long Dong Silver and Golden Hole
description: Undoubtedly the best best run of 2024. This is a Marston's pub. Dog friendly in the bar and food available. The weather will be perfect but running wellingtons are recommended. There will be a lot of mud and water.
Traditional style pub off the main road (50 Wide Lane). Open for breakfast at 09.30 and serve Sunday lunch
Local village pub serving proper beer and food
Durex Birthday run. Fabulous real ale pub. Dogs welcome in front room of pub. No meals but excellent range of fresh sandwiches
Dog friendly
St Patrick's Day Run - come along dressed as a leprechaun or at least in something green.Has a decent sized car park but you MUST REGISTER YOUR CAR on arrival. Dog friendly.
AGPU - new committee incoming? Landlady requests we park on the road as they do a carvery. R*nners trail of 5 miles mostly downhill with shortcuts for w*lkers
Running for fun in the Nottingham-Leicester-Derby area
Good beer, dog friendly and with large beer garden. Sunday lunches available

The micropub is in the pedestrian zone between the High Road and Sainsbury's. Circle up at 11 a.m. outside the pub. The hare recommends parking in the Albion Street Car Park the other side of Sainsbury's which is free on Sundays. Plenty of public transport options, Besston bus station is 5 minutes away, the railway station 15 minutes.
Wonderful countryside and close by to the former iron works at Stanton. Nice village pub serving good alea.

hares: Long Dong Silver and Golden Hole
description: An estate pub working hard to be a social focal point. Beer garden and dog friendly.Very close to Clifton Centre tram stop and several bus routes. Large car park at the front of the pub. Opens at 11am for a pre-hash drink. The trail is all downhill and beach weather is guaranteed.

Come and celebrate QH3's 1100th r*n where we started 37 years ago in Quorn village. If driving, there is a free long stay car park at Station Road, we will have a picnic and games in Stafford Orchard park next to it, please bring some nosh and liquids and a chair. Perfect 5 mile trail with shortcuts available for w*lkers.
Nice beer garden, large car park, dogs welcome in the top bar and outside
Running for fun in the Nottingham-Leicester-Derby area
Running for fun in the Nottingham-Leicester-Derby area

On Out is from the free car park on Gotham Road (by the bowls club) 200 metres from this rural pub of the year. The no. 1 bus from both Loughborough and Nottingham stops right outside the pub. Dogs are welcome on the bus, and in the pub.
Running for fun in the Nottingham-Leicester-Derby area
Part of the QH3 Matlock Away weekend -everyone welcome. Pub has no car park but there's car parking nearby at the railway station (charges apply)
Newly refurbished pub, 2 miles from M1 jnct 26. Park in car park opposite the pub
Dog-friendly pub. Real ales and cobs served. Loughborugh Rd, Whitwick, Coalville, 4 miles from M1 Jnct. 23.

***NOTE EARLIER START TIME***.Joint trail with Rutland H3.The start and On Inn is NOT a pub. It is a side road off Gaddesby Lane, which we can use to park. The side road leads to the kennels for the Quorn Hunt and is located on Google Maps as Quorn Hunt. Bring your own drinks/chairs etc.
Bardney Drive, Bulwell, Nottingham. we can expect a downhill trail, perfectly marked and in glorious sunshine.

Come and join us at the Jingle Ball run 2024 - grab your Jingling Balls and any other Christmas garb for this mainly town centre trail. We'll be going through Ashby de la Zouch town centre then out a bit, so that we will have a 5 mile trail for r*nners and a 3 mile trail for w*lkers. Halfway stop for Xmas treats etc. The dog Friendly pub doesn't have a car park but you will be able to find on-street free parking nearby

**NOTE NEW VENUE** Perfectly named pub for the last day of Christmas and the hare who has stepped in at short notice to set the trail! It serves 10 lovely ales and some decent cider. and has a small car park. The trail will be fairly short, and mostly (but not entirely) on tarmac. Wear a silly hat to protect yourself from the rain, or hang something silly from your santa hat!

hares: Long Dong Silver and Golden Hole
description: Parking on the street anywhere nearby as there are no restrictions on Sunday. Much better is to come by Nottingham City's excellent public transport. The nearest tram stops are QUEENS WALK and MEADOWS WAY WEST, both less than five minutes walk away. Buses are available, and Nottingham railway station is a 10 minutes walk. Food, beer and toilets are available at the on-inn. Dogs welcome. Forest are playing at home in the afternoon, so the town may be a little busier than usual for a Sunday - hence the non pub venue
ON-OUT from Cliffe Hill Avenue Public Car Park (NG9 7HD behind Horse and Jockey) - free parking on Sundays. CAMRA East Midlands pub of the year 2024
Durex's Big Birthday run. Pub opens at 11 a.m. and has large car park at the rear. Dog-friendly (not in restaurant)
Dog-friendly pub, hot Sunday Roast Dinner available too, when car parking log on to their computer!, carpark and pub open at 10.30 am
Our emergency hare will set a short trail from Totally Tapped, a lovely micropub at 104 Chilwell Road
Excellent range of beers. Dog-friendly

EASTER Sunday Run. People and Dog-friendly pub with car park. No meals served. Eggciting games on trail. Served by Indigo bus from Nottingham to Derby (normal Sunday/Bank Holiday service on Easter Sunday

Main trail 5 miles with a shorter route of 2.5 miles, in and around Grace Dieu woods. Nottingham Skylink bus passes within 0.5miles of the pub. Cracking pub, no food but cobs available, 4 miles from either M1 Jnct 23 or M42 Jnct 13
Popular Sunday dining pub. Need to book if you wish to stay for a meal. Landlord has asked us to park on the road rather than filling the pub car park
Running (and walking) for fun in Nottinghamshire, Leicestershire and Derbyshire
Running (and walking) for fun in Nottinghamshire, Leicestershire and Derbyshire
**Note Change of Venue - due to injury, Hare has changed venue from Stanley to Cotgrave on 30 June**
Back visiting the Gothamites. The Sun Inn has a small car park - usually plenty of parking on the road outside the pub/church. Good selection of ales and the pub does food on Sundays.
Excellent range of beers. Dog-friendly
Full address - The Kell's New Inn, Clay Lane, Peggs Green, Coleorton, Coalville LE67 8JE. Dog-friendly pub. Traditional flat Bass served straight from the barrel.
Running (and walking) for fun in Nottinghamshire, Leicestershire and Derbyshire

hares: Long Dong Silver and Golden Hole
description: Circle up in the car park of the Starting Gate, in Colwick, Dale Side Road East, Nottingham. Dog-friendly, has a big car park, and Sunday roasts from £9.49.

One of the best real ale pubs in Derby. There may be some beer left from the Dark v Light Beer Festival. If not there will still be a good interesting selection of ales on the bar. The pub is dog friendly, provided they are well behaved and on leads
ON-OUT from Cliffe Hill Avenue Public Car Park (NG9 7HD behind Horse and Jockey) - free parking on Sundays. CAMRA East Midland’s District Pub of the Year for 2024, 2023, 2022

Peggs Green is near Coleorton to the north of Coalville, located 2.5 miles from Junction 13 of the A42. The pub still serves Bass straight out of the barrel plus another couple of real ales, lagers and ciders. It is a dog-friendly pub with the car park opposite the pub.

JINGLE BALLS TRAIL. Meet in the pub (which opens at 11 am for a prehash tipple or coffee before setting off about 11:20.The trail will visit 4 or 5 establishments for refreshments with about a km of marked trail in between each stop. The pace will be relaxed, so it will take longer than a non-Jiggle Balls hash. All stops will be dog-friendly. This is an A-to-B, but the B is very close to the A and to Broadmarsh car park. Christmas dress and or headgear are mandatory. The nearest tram stop is Nottingham Station, which is connected to P and R sites from outside of the city. If you are coming by car, Broadmarsh car park is £4.50 for all-day parking. Other car parks in Nottingham are much more expensive. You can park for free a bit further away in The Meadows, as resident permits do not apply on Sundays.
Hit the New Year Hashing. Joint trail with Bullmoon Hash. Note trail is on a Saturday
Dog-friendly pub with large car park
St David's Day. Near Elvaston Castle, Derby, a pub with a big car park and 5 real ales. A rarely hashed area so virgin trails promised. 5 miles r*nners trail, plus a shorter walkers route.
April Hash and QH3 AGM. Gem of a craft beer and real ale micropub

The micro-pub is dog-friendly and serves 8 real ales plus keg and ciders, plus hot food and cakes. The pub doesn't have a car park so suggest parking on Kingfisher Close. R*nners trail will be exactly 5-miles and there's also 3-mile route for walkers, both of which feature virgin paths and bluebell woods.
Mid-summer's Day Run. Note this is a trail on the 3rd Sunday of June

Holly Bush Inn is a traditional 17th century village inn, where highwayman Dick Turpin is reported to have frequented on his travels. They claim nothing comes close to our pork pie and a pint! No carpark so just park randomly on the road.

The QH3 summer picnic returns to Rushcliffe Country Park. As previously, we'll meet/start at a 'back' entrance to the park where the railway crosses Asher Lane (opposite the entrance to Leys Farm, Post Code NG11 6JX). Parking on Asher Lane is free but after 11:00 spaces tend to be further away from the entrance. The trail will be approx. five miles with plenty of options for shortcuts. The On Inn/Picnic spot will be a 1-minute walk from the entrance. Good shade from trees and some benches available. If the weather requires it, the hares will erect a Gazebo. Those that can should bring chairs to sit on. Bring your own drink and picnic - usual format bring extra food to share.
Very experienced hare team - must be a cracking trail. Hash trail of 5 miles and a walkers' option of under 3 miles
First time QH3 has been to this On Inn not far from Ilkeston. Good car park, dog-friendly and plenty of good trail opportunities.
Pub is dog-friendly and has a car park.Dogs will need to be on a lead throughout the trail
